task.title: Start generated release notes at the line's previous release
task.description: Follow-up from the review of "Cut patch releases to an older line without releasing main" (PR #175, 2026-10-10). scripts/publish-release.sh (~201-205) publishes with `gh release create --generate-notes` and no `--notes-start-tag` when a release has no changelog entry, so GitHub picks the previous release itself. For an older-line patch such as v0.5.2 cut from maint/v0.5 after v0.6.0 exists, GitHub may compare against v0.6.0 rather than v0.5.1, giving backward-looking notes for a quiet backport. Verify GitHub's actual selection rule (docs for generate-notes / previous_tag_name) and, for a stable release, pass --notes-start-tag set to the newest stable tag on the same line that orders before the release (newest_release_tag with the LINE filter from PR #175); for the first release of a new minor, the previous release overall. Pre-releases must keep today's behavior unless clearly wrong too. Assert the gh stub's recorded calls for: newest ordinary patch, new minor, older-line patch, pre-release.
